newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sells 20 bln bolivars of TEM bills.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sells 20 bln bolivars of TEM bills.

text.p: Venezuela's Central Bank said it sold 10 billion bolivars of 180-day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills at a price of 102.72 pct.
The 180-day bills carried a 34.12 percent coupon.

The bank also sold five billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 35.52 percent coupon at a price of 101.89 percent, and five billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 36.99 percent coupon at an average price of 101.58 percent.

According to a preliminary calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula, the yield on the notes fell to 27.93 percent for the 180-day TEMs, to 32.37 percent for the 269-day notes, and to 34.85 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
Yields for 180-, 269-, and 358-day bills sold at last week's auction were 34.12 percent, 37.71 percent and 38.79 percent respectively.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
